INSTANT.rule: timingType itself encodes zero duration; do not write baseDurationTicks:0 or durationMs:0.

FORMULA_DURATION.constraint: Formula must resolve in the record's clock domain; current route formulas resolve to SIMULATION_TIME ticks.

RESPONSE_WINDOW.constraint: responseWindowTicks is a positive integer unless a future real-world response type explicitly defines another unit.

REAL_WORLD_DEADLINE.constraint: durationMs is a positive integer number of milliseconds.

actionCatalogSchema.unitRule: Tick-named fields may appear only on SIMULATION_TIME timing values. Millisecond-named duration fields may appear only on REAL_WORLD_TIME duration/deadline values.
actionCatalogSchema.instantRule: Instant records are unit-neutral and carry no zero-valued tick/millisecond duration field.

authoritySplit.processedSimulationAuthority: worldTick and all domain state committed through that tick
authoritySplit.rule: Real time may accrue ahead of processed simulation. The difference is an explicit durable backlog, never implicit in wall-clock arithmetic.

invariants: worldTick <= accruedTargetWorldTick.
pendingWholeTicks = accruedTargetWorldTick - worldTick.
lastAccrualAtMs may advance even when pendingWholeTicks > 0.
Processing worldTick never changes lastAccrualAtMs or re-accrues real time.
Accruing additional real time never silently marks unprocessed world ticks as processed.
No simulation tick is considered processed until all authoritative effects for that tick have committed.

afterFirst64TickProcessingSlice.lastAccrualAtMs: unchanged from the already-committed accrual cursor

accrualBacklogContract.casRule: Accrual-state updates and simulation-processing updates both use the existing stateVersion/CAS path. On conflict, reload all five temporal fields and authoritative domain state; never recompute from a stale lastAccrualAtMs or stale accruedTargetWorldTick.

reinforcementTemporalContract.canonicalPostMigrationRule: Cross-territory troop reinforcement is a physical FORCE_TRANSIT action with movementPurpose REINFORCE.
reinforcementTemporalContract.legacyCurrentBehavior: REP-WARS-3 currently has an instant garrison-add REINFORCE handler.

commit: Validate source territory/garrison, destination territory, route, ownership/alliance requirements, available troop quantity, and action eligibility.
Detach the committed troop quantity from the source garrison into a uniquely identified force/formation.
Acquire EXCLUSIVE_ENTITY/QUANTITY reservations atomically with the commitment.
Create FORCE_TRANSIT with movementPurpose REINFORCE and completionTick derived from SHARED_ROUTE_DURATION(route).
commandLifecycle.transit: Troops are unavailable at both source and destination while in transit except through the authoritative in-transit force record.
arrival: If valid, merge the reinforcing force into the destination garrison as an immediate arrival consequence.
If invalid, transition through explicit failure/interruption/reroute behavior rather than teleporting the troops.

sameTerritoryException.rule: A purely local reassignment inside the same territory may remain instantaneous if no territory connection is crossed and the operation is explicitly classified as local garrison management rather than cross-territory REINFORCE.

marketDeliveryTemporalMapping.rule: A future physical market-delivery flow must create RESOURCE_SHIPMENT with purpose MARKET_DELIVERY. It may not introduce a third independent transport-duration system.
marketDeliveryTemporalMapping.arrival: On valid arrival, consume the shipment manifest and apply the market/destination delivery consequence atomically using the normal resource-shipment arrival path.

productionTemporalCutover.purpose: Move an existing pre-temporal REP-WARS-3 world onto the canonical fixed-point time authority without inventing retroactive simulation time or trusting the legacy unwired wall-clock watermark.

migrationMarker.rule: If temporalAuthorityVersion >= 1, cutover has already completed and initialization must never run again.

capturedCutoverTime.rule: Capture once per cutover attempt and use the same value for every migration calculation in the successful atomic cutover.

orderedCutoverAlgorithm: Load the authoritative pre-temporal GameState under the existing stateVersion/CAS rules.
If temporalAuthorityVersion >= 1, do not rerun cutover.
Capture migrationServerNowMs once from the authoritative server clock.

While legacy clocks are still readable, migrate all legacy time-sensitive domain state: invasion response time, defense-workout deadlines, event timing, movement, construction, commitments, cooldowns, and tutorial timing.
Any migrated REAL_WORLD_TIME deadline already due at migrationServerNowMs must remain due; migration may not grant a fresh full duration.
Keep the existing worldTick exactly as the fully processed simulation cursor.
Initialize presence/rate state at migrationServerNowMs. If a valid authenticated gameplay-session lease exists or is issued at cutover, ONLINE begins at that boundary; otherwise OFFLINE begins there.
Set temporalAuthorityVersion = 1 and persist migrated domain state, canonical clock fields, presence state, frontier/gates, and the migration marker in one CAS commit.
Only after that commit succeeds may canonical accrual begin from migrationServerNowMs forward.

legacyLastProcessedAtMs.rule: Do not use pre-cutover GameState.lastProcessedAtMs as the initial canonical accrual cursor for the current migration baseline.
legacyLastProcessedAtMs.allowedUse: Legacy diagnostic metadata only unless a future migration proves a particular value came from the canonical production time authority.

productionTemporalCutover.noRetroactiveAccrualRule: Canonical accrual intentionally begins at migrationServerNowMs. Real time before that boundary is not converted into new-engine ticks.
idempotency: A failed CAS commit leaves old authoritative state unchanged; reload and recompute.
A successful cutover may never reset its canonical accrual cursor on later hydration.
cutoverInvariants: Immediately after successful cutover: worldTick == accruedTargetWorldTick.
subTickMicroticks == 0 and accrualDivisionRemainder == 0 at the cutover boundary.
No pre-cutover wall-clock interval is double-counted.
Legacy time-sensitive state is migrated before legacy clock semantics are discarded.

commandAdmissionContract.purpose: Preserve a mutating command's temporal position and first authoritative server receipt time when catch-up needs multiple slices or retries.
commandAdmissionContract.scope: All mutating gameplay commands; deadline-sensitive commands use additional boundary ordering.

idempotencyKey.source: Reuse an existing stable client request identifier if present; otherwise add a client-generated opaque unique commandId to the mutating command envelope and reuse it unchanged on retries.
idempotencyKey.sameIdSamePayload: Resume/return the existing admission or terminal result; never execute twice.
idempotencyKey.sameIdDifferentPayload: Reject as IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH with no gameplay mutation.

commandAdmissionContract.firstReceiptAuthority: firstServerReceivedAtMs is server-captured on first successful durable admission and is immutable on every retry.
admissionAlgorithm: Authenticate/authorize the envelope and validate basic shape without applying the gameplay mutation.
After server-side schema parsing/normalization, compute payloadHash and payloadHashVersion using payloadFingerprint. Never trust a client-supplied hash.

Look up (worldId, actorId, commandId). If an admission exists with the same payloadHashVersion and payloadHash, resume/return it. If either fingerprint version/hash differs, reject with IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH.
Accrue canonical time exactly through T using authoritative rate history. Accrual may move accruedTargetWorldTick but not worldTick.
Snapshot admittedTargetWorldTick = accruedTargetWorldTick and admittedSubTickMicroticks = subTickMicroticks as of T.
Persist the accrual update and new ADMITTED_WAITING_FOR_CATCHUP admission atomically under CAS. Temporal guarantees begin only after this commit succeeds.
Process toward the command fence. If processing budget ends, return accepted/pending keyed by commandId and keep the admission durable.
When the command temporal position is reached and all earlier obligations are resolved, mark READY_TO_EXECUTE.
Perform full domain validation against authoritative state at that temporal position.
Apply the domain mutation at most once and terminalize the admission in the same authoritative commit.
Retries with the same commandId resume/return the same result.

temporalFence.rule: A pending admitted command is a processing fence. Accrual may move beyond it, but simulation processing may not cross its admittedTargetWorldTick before the command executes/rejects at its proper position.
temporalFence.multipleCommands: Order pending admissions by firstServerReceivedAtMs ascending, then commandId ascending. Commands in the same simulation tick execute in that order with no invented tick between them.
temporalFence.fractionalPosition: admittedSubTickMicroticks records fractional position; whole-tick simulation state advances only on ticks. Within one tick, firstServerReceivedAtMs then commandId controls order.

deadlineSensitiveCommands.rule: Deadline validity uses immutable firstServerReceivedAtMs, never a later retry time.
exactRealWorldDeadlineOrdering: If a command-specific rule explicitly makes the exact real-world deadline inclusive, an admitted command with firstServerReceivedAtMs == boundaryAtMs executes before that matching expiry gate.
Otherwise the real-world expiry gate at the same boundaryAtMs resolves before the command.
Use commandId/boundary stable IDs for deterministic ties within one priority.
deadlineSensitiveCommands.lateRule: If firstServerReceivedAtMs is after the authoritative deadline, catch-up or retry cannot make the command timely.

commandAdmissionContract.acceptanceResponseRule: The server may return accepted/pending after durable admission even if execution waits on catch-up; return commandId for idempotent polling/retry.

failureAndRestart.beforeAdmissionCommit: No temporal guarantee exists until admission commits.
failureAndRestart.afterAdmissionBeforeExecution: Restart reconstructs pending admissions/fences and preserves firstServerReceivedAtMs.
failureAndRestart.afterDomainMutationCommit: Terminalize admission atomically with the gameplay mutation so retry cannot double-apply.

invariants: No commandId executes its gameplay mutation more than once.
No retry changes firstServerReceivedAtMs.
No scheduler processing crosses an earlier pending command fence.
Terminalization and associated gameplay mutation are atomic.
Client-authored timestamps never determine deadline validity.
Receipt-time preservation does not bypass normal domain validation.

fingerprintInput.commandType: canonical command type after command-name normalization
fingerprintInput.payload: validated and schema-normalized gameplay payload after server-side parsing/default normalization, with only gameplay-semantic command arguments included

rules: Serialize the fingerprintInput object, not the raw HTTP body.
Object keys are sorted lexicographically by Unicode code point at every nesting level.
Array element order is preserved exactly because array order may be gameplay-semantic.
Strings are serialized as standard JSON strings with deterministic JSON escaping.
Booleans and null use standard JSON literals.
Numbers must first pass command-schema validation/normalization; serialize them in the server's canonical finite JSON-number representation and reject NaN/Infinity.
Omitted optional values remain omitted after schema normalization; explicit null remains null only when the command schema treats null as semantically distinct.
Do not include properties unknown to the canonical command schema.
canonicalSerialization.normalizationRule: Semantically equivalent accepted inputs must be normalized by the command schema before serialization. Do not case-fold, reorder arrays, or otherwise change values unless that command's schema already defines that normalization.

payloadFingerprint.retryComparison: For an existing (worldId, actorId, commandId), recompute COMMAND_FINGERPRINT_V1 on the retry. Matching version+hash resumes/returns the admission; any mismatch is IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH.
payloadFingerprint.versioningRule: Never reinterpret a persisted payloadHash under a different canonicalization algorithm. A future fingerprint format must use a new payloadHashVersion and define migration/compatibility explicitly.

recurringScheduleAnchors.principle: Global recurring sweeps use a canonical modular phase anchored to simulation tick 0. Their cadence alone is not sufficient; the phase is part of authoritative temporal behavior.
recurringScheduleAnchors.dueFormula: A global sweep with cadence C and anchor A is due at tick T when T > A and (T - A) mod C == 0.
recurringScheduleAnchors.nextBoundaryFormula: nextBoundaryTick(currentTick, cadence, anchor=0) = anchor + ceil((currentTick + 1 - anchor) / cadence) * cadence
migrationRule: Do not replay global sweep boundaries at or before the cutover worldTick.
At cutover, compute the first future AI Director sweep as the smallest tick > worldTick divisible by 5.
At cutover, compute the first future world-event eligibility sweep as the smallest tick > worldTick divisible by 10.
Legacy lastAiDecisionTick may remain diagnostic metadata but does not define the new global AI sweep phase.

Persisted active commitments, post-action reassessment boundaries, event states, cooldowns, and other already-scheduled boundaries remain authoritative and are not delayed merely to align with a global sweep.
recurringScheduleAnchors.newWorldRule: A new world beginning at worldTick 0 has its first global AI Director sweep at tick 5 and first world-event eligibility sweep at tick 10.
recurringScheduleAnchors.catchUpRule: Live processing and catch-up must enumerate or safely skip the exact same anchored sweep ticks. Skipping remains legal only under the subsystem-specific proof rules and may not change RNG draw count/order.
recurringScheduleAnchors.sameTickRule: When anchored sweeps coincide with other boundaries, canonical sameTickOrder determines subsystem execution. The anchor determines WHEN a sweep is due, not its priority inside the tick.

syntheticTimeAuthority.purpose: Provide deterministic dev/test/CLI simulation-time advancement without bypassing the canonical accrued-target backlog or scheduler.

authorityModes.REAL_TIME_PRODUCTION: Authoritative production mode. Real server time plus presence/rate segments accrues simulation time. Synthetic ADVANCE_WORLD is unavailable.
authorityModes.SYNTHETIC_TEST: Internal test/CLI mode. Explicit synthetic tick grants replace production wall-clock accrual for simulation-time advancement.

syntheticTimeAuthority.modeIsolationRule: One world-processing session uses one time authority mode. Do not mix production real-time accrual and synthetic tick grants as simultaneous authorities for the same interval.

algorithm: Validate requestedSyntheticTicks is a non-negative integer.
Do not create or rewrite ONLINE/OFFLINE rate history.
Process the resulting backlog through the exact canonical catchUpScheduler, same-tick ordering, temporal fences, reservations, RNG ordering, and persistence semantics used by production time.
A single invocation may stop after a bounded processing slice; accruedTargetWorldTick retains all remaining synthetic backlog.

syntheticTimeAuthority.processingSliceRelationship: The 64-tick processing slice is not a maximum synthetic grant. A test may grant more than 64 ticks; the scheduler still processes/checkpoints in bounded slices.
syntheticTimeAuthority.realWorldDeadlineRule: ADVANCE_WORLD advances SIMULATION_TIME only. It does not move REAL_WORLD_TIME and therefore does not by itself expire presence leases, workout-session clocks, or defense-workout real-world deadlines. Tests that need real-world progression must advance/inject the test server clock separately.
syntheticTimeAuthority.determinismRule: Granting N synthetic ticks and draining the canonical backlog must produce the same simulation state as N equivalent canonical simulation ticks under identical commands, persisted decisions, and RNG inputs.
syntheticTimeAuthority.persistenceRule: Synthetic grants modify the same persisted accruedTargetWorldTick backlog as real-time accrual would, but only in an explicitly synthetic test environment.

attackerCooldown.reason: 30 ticks better matches the established strategic timing ladder: movement 2-5, ordinary construction 6-16, City 24, human response windows 30, and City L3 30. It remains substantial without making an ordinary resolved engagement share the 60-tick world-scale duration/cooldown tier.
